notes: Account background: large integrated health system with telemetry and triage chat across ER and primary care; strict PHI residency requirements for EU and Canada clinics.
Primary driver: replace brittle on-prem inference cluster with predictable Dedicated capacity and clear SLOs; minimize tail latency for clinician workflows.

Workshop outputs (high level): baseline steady-state QPS = 110-140 qps across US regions, average response tokens ~75, average request tokens ~20, resulting baseline token/sec ~10k-12k. Peak bursts 3-4x for morning triage windows (target peak planning at 420-560 qps).
Latency targets: p50 < 60ms for lightweight assistant turns, p95 <= 250ms for standard chat responses (95th must include KV cache hits). 99th target discussed as soft requirement during outages.

Desired throughput guarantee: support sustained 12k tokens/sec per region with headroom for 1.5x burst for scheduled events. Customer prefers committed reserved GPU pool with autoscale to handle bursts via pre-warmed nodes rather than cold start scaling.

Model preferences: curated open models (instruction-tuned LLaMA variants) for cost and control; willing to evaluate 8-bit quantized variants for non-critical summarization pipelines, but clinical triage requires float16/ BF16 precision and provenance.
Operational needs: token-level billing visibility, per-route latency SLOs, tracing hooks for audit, and HIPAA-friendly BAAs. Encryption at rest with customer KMS and strict key lifecycle policies.
SLA negotiation notes: procurement pushing for 99.95% uptime, penalty caps, and runbook for fallback to hosted API in cross-region failover. Legal requested sample SLA language (see drive link).

Sizing proposal considerations: recommend 6-10 H100-equivalent GPUs per US region for committed pool (steady-state capacity), with 2-3 warm spare nodes for burst; traffic routing by policy to allow EU patient data to remain within EU private deployment. Include autoscale policy that uses burst credit rather than unlimited on-demand expansion.

Open technical questions: expected average sequence length for reranking flows (we captured a subset but need production logs), confirmation of KV cache reuse rate (affects memory planning), and retention window for audit logs (customer requires 7 years for certain records).
Quotes from stakeholders: CTO: 'We need predictable latency for the triage flow — a 300ms blip is unacceptable during ER hours.' Head of Security: 'Show us key provenance and how long logs are kept.'

Next workshop action items: SE to produce GPU sizing matrix (tokens/sec per GPU for proposed model family), product to produce sample SLA with regional residency clauses, AE to align procurement calendar for Jan decision
